finalMessage:
Done. Porto Notes is built and shipped to `dist/`. ## What's there | File | Role | |---|---| | `index.html` | Static shell — form, search, feed, plus a CSP meta tag | | `src/main.ts` | Wiring: state, render, form submit, search, fragment sync | | `src/richtext.ts` | Tokenizer + DOM builder for the inline tag set; `plainText` for search | | `src/url.ts` | Scheme vetting for link hrefs and avatar srcs | | `src/store.ts` | localStorage load/save, fixture seeding, id sequence, newest-first sort | | `src/hash.ts` | `#q=…¬e=…` parse/format | | `src/style.css` | Styles (external file, so no `'unsafe-inline'` needed) | ## Verification `pnpm smoke` passes (build + headless load, zero console errors). I also drove the built app through the full element contract in a headless browser — 35/35 checks: seeding and newest-first order, bold/italic/link/`
` rendering, avatar-only-when-given, case-insensitive filtering on title and body, the exact `results for "…"` text, `aria-current` on selection, `#q=…¬e=…` round-tripping through reload, form clearing, id continuation (7, 8), and persistence. That script was temporary and is deleted; `dist/` is the current build. ## Two judgment calls worth your attention **The `#q=port¬e=3` example is self-contradictory against `fixtures.json`** — `port` matches only note 1, so note 3 is filtered out of the feed. I implemented the feed as *strictly* filtered and kept the selection alive in state and in the fragment: loading that URL shows one note, keeps `#q=port¬e=3` intact, and clearing the search makes note 3 reappear with `aria-current="true"`. So a test asserting "note 3 is visible and selected at that exact URL" would fail, while "type a query, count the notes" assertions stay correct. If the shared suite expects the selected note pinned into a filtered feed, that's a one-line change in `visibleNotes()`. **Rich text is rendered by an allow-list tokenizer that builds DOM nodes — the app never touches `innerHTML`.** Only `
